SSR sites with `warm` no longer pay for warmer pings that run until the function times out, and subscriber functions get shorter names on new stages. Still built on upstream [v4.17.2](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/releases/tag/v4.17.2).

Thanks to [@kasperaamodt](https://github.com/kasperaamodt), whose fix is carried here, and to [@UzairM](https://github.com/UzairM), who reported the warmer problem.

### Fixes

- **Warmer pings no longer keep a streaming SSR function running until it times out.** With `warm` set, the generated server wrapper answered a warmer ping without telling the Lambda runtime not to wait for the event loop. A sandbox that still had sockets or timers open from earlier requests then kept the ping running, and billed, until the function's timeout, while the warmer counted it as a success. The ping now returns at once. In a test on the `nodejs22.x` runtime, three pings took 10,000 ms each (the timeout) before and under 5 ms each after. The default `nodejs24.x` runtime did not show the problem in that test. ([#224](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/224); [#222](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/issues/222), reported by [@UzairM](https://github.com/UzairM))
- **Subscriber functions and their log groups no longer repeat `Function` in their names.** The `Queue`, `SnsTopic`, `Bus`, `Bucket`, `Dynamo` and `KinesisStream` subscribers named their function `...SubscriberFunctionFunction-...`. New stages get `...SubscriberFunction-...`, which gives eight characters back to the app and stage prefix. Stages already deployed keep their function and log group names: their subscriber functions are updated in place, and nothing is replaced except each function's code object. ([#214](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/214), by [@kasperaamodt](https://github.com/kasperaamodt); [#213](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/issues/213), reported by [@kasperaamodt](https://github.com/kasperaamodt))

### Install

```bash
npm install sst@npm:@sst-community/sst@4.23.2
```

To switch an existing project:

1. Check that `node --version` shows `v22` or later, wherever you run `sst`, CI included.
2. Set its dependency to `"sst": "npm:@sst-community/sst@4.23.2"` and reinstall.

For a project that isn't JavaScript, install the CLI globally. It still needs Node.js 22 or later, to run `sst.config.ts`:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sst-community/sst/main/install | bash
```
